post.description:
Create a new payment. Supports PIX and boleto, in headless or hosted mode, and card through the hosted checkout only. Requires an idempotency key.

Card payments are not accepted through the API. A `card` object, `CARD` in `methods` in headless mode (`mode` omitted or `headless`), or any of these fields at the top level of the body: `deviceInfo`, `remoteIp`, `holderInfo`, `authorizeOnly`, `creditCard`, `creditCardHolderInfo`, `creditCardToken`, `installmentCount`, `installmentValue`, `totalValue`, is rejected with `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API`, even without a valid API key, and the card data is not stored or logged.

To charge a card, create the payment with `mode: hosted` and `CARD` in `methods` (`["CARD"]`, or `["PIX", "CARD"]` to let the payer choose), with an `amount` of at least R$ 5.00, and redirect the payer to the returned `checkoutUrl`. The checkout collects the card, accepts credit cards in a single installment and debit cards, and runs 3D Secure itself. The result arrives as `PAYMENT_CONFIRMED`, `PAYMENT_PAID`, `PAYMENT_EXPIRED` or `PAYMENT_CANCELLED`; you can also poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}`.

Send `items` to sell several lines in one payment, `couponCode` to apply a coupon, and, on a hosted payment, `itemsQuantityEditable`, `orderBump` and `upsell`. The response carries `items`, `subtotal`, `discount` and `coupon`. A coupon that discounts the whole amount completes the payment as `FREE`, with no charge.

parameters.name: X-Split-Platform-Key
parameters.description: API key of an approved split platform, sent as the key itself, without `Bearer`, in the environment of the key in `Authorization`: `ypk_live_` in production, `ypk_test_` in sandbox. It lets the platform named in `splits[]` connect the seller on this call, with no dashboard invitation: the relationship is recorded as `ACCEPTED` with the platform's fee cap and the payment is created. The connection works in production and in sandbox under the same fee cap, and only a production connection notifies the seller. The header is read only when exactly one recipient in `splits[]` has no accepted relationship with your company, and ignored otherwise. A key that is unknown, revoked or expired, is from the other environment, lacks the `payments:write` scope, is used from outside its IP allowlist or belongs to your own company returns `403 SPLIT_PLATFORM_KEY_INVALID`. A valid key whose company is not that recipient, or is not an approved platform, connects nobody: the request follows the regular flow and returns `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`. Send it from a server only. See the Split platforms guide.

400.description: Validation failed, or the request was refused. `CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API`: the request carries card data or asks for `CARD` in headless mode; card payments go through the hosted checkout only. It takes precedence over validation and authentication errors, so it is returned even without a valid API key. Split-specific codes: `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `SPLIT_SELF_RECIPIENT`, `SPLIT_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_NET`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REQUEST_LIMIT`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_REVOKED`, `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_INACTIVE`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_APPROVED`, `SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH`, `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED`, `SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED`, `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_PENDING` is returned for every recipient that cannot receive a split yet apart from a pair that declined an invitation from your company or was revoked, identical whether the company ID exists or not; `SPLIT_RELATIONSHIP_DECLINED` carries `details.recipients`, the company IDs that declined; `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_INACTIVE`, `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_NOT_APPROVED` and `SPLIT_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH` are returned only for a recipient that had already accepted the relationship. `SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED`: a split to an approved split platform is above its fee cap, with `details.recipientCompanyId` and `details.feeCap`. `SPLIT_PLATFORM_SUSPENDED`: the recipient is a platform connected with a fee cap whose approval was withdrawn, with `details.recipientCompanyId`. `SPLIT_PARTNER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`: a platform connection through `X-Split-Platform-Key` would take your company past its limit of active partners, with `details.limit`. Cart codes: `AMOUNT_ITEMS_MISMATCH`, `amount` is not the sum of `items`, with `details.amount` and `details.itemsTotal` (a string such as `"159.70"`); `ITEM_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`, an item `productId` is not a product of your account in this environment; `OFFER_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`, the same for `orderBump` or `upsell`; `UPSELL_AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH`, the upsell costs more than the payment `amount` after the coupon; `COUPON_INVALID`, `couponCode` cannot be used on this payment, one answer for every reason; `AMOUNT_TOO_HIGH`, the sum of `items` is above R$ 1,000,000.00; `MINIMUM_AMOUNT_FOR_CARD_OR_BOLETO`, the sum of `items`, or a headless boleto amount after the coupon, is below R$ 5.00. `orderBump` or `upsell` in headless mode returns `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `OFFERS_REQUIRE_HOSTED` in the message. `PROVIDER_REJECTED` means the payment was refused and the message is generic; a refused boleto payment is recorded as `CANCELLED`. Note that a missing `X-Idempotency-Key` is rejected before the error envelope is applied and returns the flat shape `{ statusCode, error, message, code }` with code `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`.

502.description: Code `PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE`. On a boleto payment the outcome of the charge is not known yet: the payment stays `PROCESSING`, with `methodData: null`, until it is resolved, which can take 15 minutes or more, and then either continues normally or ends `CANCELLED`. This `502` is stored for the `X-Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key returns the same `502` for 24 hours and never submits a second charge. To recover the payment, repeat the request once with the same `externalId` and a new `X-Idempotency-Key`: the response is the existing payment, with its `id`, and no new charge is submitted. Then poll `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` until it leaves `PROCESSING`. On a PIX payment the charge was not created and the payment is recorded as `CANCELLED`: retry with a new `externalId`.

503.description: Codes: `PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE`, the charge was not created and the payment is recorded as `CANCELLED`, so retry later with a new `externalId`; `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, the requested payment method is temporarily disabled.

post.description: Issue a full or partial refund for a paid payment. Requires an idempotency key. A payment can be refunded once, fully or partially: after a partial refund a new refund is rejected with `REFUND_ALREADY_PERFORMED`, and after a full refund with `ALREADY_REFUNDED`. While a refund is being processed, a new one is rejected with `400 REFUND_IN_PROGRESS`. A partial refund additionally requires a settled payment and a processing route that supports partial refunds; otherwise it is rejected with `PARTIAL_REFUND_NOT_SUPPORTED`. When the payment carries splits, the refund is apportioned: every party is debited in proportion to what it received, including the originating company, and partial refunds use the same proportions. `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE_FOR_REFUND` is evaluated against the originating company's share only — a recipient that has already withdrawn its share goes negative instead of blocking the refund, and the shortfall is never moved onto the originating company. When the refund takes the counted volume of your verified CPF or CNPJ below a rewards prize that YuvexPay approved for it, the processing fee is not returned: your balance is debited the full amount returned to the payer, and the kept fee, debited from the originating company only, can take the available balance negative. A `FREE` payment was never charged and returns `400 INVALID_STATUS`.

post.description:
Create a PIX withdrawal to transfer BRL funds from your YuvexPay balance. Requires an idempotency key.

The PIX key type (CPF, CNPJ, e-mail, phone, or random key) is detected automatically from `destination.pixKey` — you do not need to declare it. `INVALID_PIX_KEY` covers format only. Whether the key exists on the PIX network is not checked before acceptance: depending on when the network rejects, a well-formed key that belongs to nobody surfaces either as a synchronous `400 PROVIDER_ERROR` on this call or later as a `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED` webhook.

The creditor document sent to the PIX network is resolved in three steps, in order: (1) `destination.recipientDocument` when you send it; (2) the PIX key itself when `destination.pixKey` is a CPF or CNPJ key; (3) your own verified tax id — company CNPJ for business accounts, owner CPF for individual accounts. Step 3 is a fallback, not a default: if you pay a third party on an e-mail, phone or random key and omit `destination.recipientDocument`, the network is told your own document is the creditor, and the payout may be rejected downstream by the receiving institution.

Withdrawals may be blocked outside business hours or if your account has restrictions.

`creditorDocumentSource` is a dashboard-only field and is not accepted here: sending it returns `400 CREDITOR_DOCUMENT_SOURCE_NOT_SUPPORTED` rather than being silently ignored. Use `destination.recipientDocument` to put a specific document on the payout.

Retrieve a single withdrawal by its ID.

Return the current BRL balance for the company associated with the API key. The endpoint takes no parameters — the company is always derived from the API key. The four balance buckets are independent and additive: `available` (settled funds free to use; a withdrawal is also bounded by `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`), `frozen` (set aside for in-flight withdrawals, refunds, or operational holds — not currently withdrawable), `held` (confirmed but pending settlement), and `reserved` (a rolling reserve withheld from settled funds and released on a schedule — not currently withdrawable). The total account balance is `available + frozen + held + reserved`. A split credit received from another YuvexPay company follows your own rolling reserve policy, not the originating company's. A sandbox API key always returns zeros, since sandbox transactions do not accumulate to a real balance.

get.description: Generate an account statement for a date range. Maximum range is 90 days. The statement is built from the real-money ledger, which sandbox transactions never touch, so a sandbox key always receives an empty statement with zero balances. Split credits received from other YuvexPay companies, and the proportional debits taken back on a refund or MED, appear here. Besides `GET /v1/balance`, this is the only public record a recipient has of a split: the payment itself belongs to the originating company and is not readable by the recipient. The price of a recovery kit appears as a debit labelled `Kit de recuperação`. The fee of a free order, a payment a coupon covered in full, appears as a debit labelled `Taxa de pedido gratuito`.

get.description: Return the companies your account may split payments with, in both directions, for the environment of the API key. A pair is created in the dashboard: the originating company invites the recipient by company ID and the recipient accepts. There is no API to invite, accept, decline or revoke — accepting is a human act. The one exception is an approved split platform, which connects a seller on the seller's first payment by sending `X-Split-Platform-Key` on `POST /v1/payments`, in production and in sandbox. Use this endpoint to discover which `companyId` values you may send as `recipientCompanyId` in `splits[]`: only a partner whose `status` is `ACCEPTED` is usable. The list carries the live row for each pair, plus the most recent answered row for a pair that has no live one, so a rejected or revoked pair is still visible. Every partner is returned in one response, newest first, unless `limit` is sent: then at most `limit` relationships are read per call, a page can carry fewer partners than `limit`, and you pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. Requires the `payments:read` scope.

The payment expired before being completed. For boleto this is not always terminal — a boleto paid on or shortly after its due date can settle late, producing a `PAYMENT_PAID` afterwards for the same charge.

IdempotencyKey.description: A unique string to ensure the request is processed only once. Must be unique per request. Valid for 24 hours. Successful (`2xx`) responses are stored and replayed for the key. On `POST /v1/payments`, a `502 PROVIDER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` for a boleto payment is stored and replayed too: to recover that payment, repeat the request once with the same `externalId` and a new key. A retry of an earlier card payment request now returns `400 CARD_PAYMENTS_NOT_AVAILABLE_VIA_API` instead of the stored response (`201` or `502`): recover that payment with `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}`, or with a create request with the same `externalId`, `mode: "hosted"` and `methods: ["CARD"]`, no `card` object or card fields, and a new key.

Must be a company other than your own, unique within `splits`, in the same environment as the payment (an approved split platform connected in sandbox is the exception), approved (KYC, plus KYB for a business), and it must have accepted split payments from your company. An approved split platform that is not connected yet can be named when the request carries its key in `X-Split-Platform-Key`. A split to an approved platform is limited by its fee cap (`SPLIT_FEE_CAP_EXCEEDED`).

Any other field that is not a string or is longer than its limit fails the request with `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. passFeeToPayer.description: Whether the YuvexPay fee should be added on top of `amount` and charged to the payer instead of being deducted from the merchant's net. When omitted, the company-level `passFeeToPayerDefault` setting applies. Note: payments with a resolved amount below R$1,00 are always charged to the payer regardless of this value (forced passthrough to keep merchant net positive). The final decision is reflected back as `feePassedToPayer` on the Payment object. On a hosted payment the fee is computed again, at the rate of the method the payer picks, card included; the checkout shows each method with its own total. A payment that completes as `FREE` never passes a fee.

splits.description: Share part of this payment with other YuvexPay companies when it settles. Optional. The maximum number of entries is the recipient limit configured for your account — three by default, and support can raise it; going over it returns `SPLIT_RECIPIENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The sum of the splits must not exceed `netAmount`, otherwise the request fails with `SPLIT_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_NET` and nothing is clamped. The YuvexPay fee is always yours and is never apportioned. Splits are set only at creation: there is no endpoint to add, edit or remove one afterwards.

recoveryKit.description: Turn the recovery kit on (`true`) or off (`false`) for this payment. When omitted, the account default applies (Ativar por padrão on the Kit de recuperação card in the dashboard, off until turned on). The kit e-mails a payer who filled in the hosted checkout and did not pay: up to 5 e-mails at the delays set for the account, 15 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours unless changed, plus one about 10 minutes before a PIX code expires, sent only while the payment can still be paid. It starts when the hosted checkout saves the payer's details, or when the checkout is first opened for a payment whose customer already has them, so it does nothing on a headless payment. The kit price, shown in the dashboard, is debited once, when the first e-mail is sent, even if the balance goes negative. Sandbox payments never get a kit: `recoveryKit.enabled` is `false` on them. The result is returned as `recoveryKit` on the Payment object.

couponCode.description: Coupon to apply, case-insensitive. A code that does not exist, is inactive, outside its validity window, out of uses, over the per-payer limit for `customer.email`, gives no discount on this order, or is sent with a `FIXED` split returns `400 COUPON_INVALID`, one answer for every reason. amount.description: The NET amount in BRL — exactly what the recipient receives. The platform fee is added on top, never deducted: your balance is debited `amount + feeAmount` (returned as `grossAmount`), and that gross is what counts against `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, the daily/nightly limits and the per-transaction cap. The R$10.00 minimum is compared against `amount` (the net); it is the floor the platform never goes below, and the value that actually applies to you is `minAmount` from `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`. The 1,000,000 ceiling is a request-validation bound, not your limit — the per-transaction cap that applies to your account is returned by `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`.

A key that matches none of those shapes is rejected with `INVALID_PIX_KEY`.

Send it whenever the destination key belongs to someone other than you. Omitting it on a third-party e-mail, phone or random key makes the network see your own document as creditor. If `pixKey` is itself a CPF or CNPJ key, this field must agree with it or the request is rejected with `RECIPIENT_DOCUMENT_MISMATCH`.

quantity.description: Quantity. The payer may have changed it on the hosted checkout when the payment was created with `itemsQuantityEditable: true`.

kind.description: `ITEM`: a line you sent in `items`. `ORDER_BUMP`: the order bump the payer ticked. `UPSELL`: the line of a payment created by a post-purchase upsell.

PaymentCoupon.description: The coupon applied to the payment, or `null`.

amount.description: Amount in BRL before any fee passed to the payer: `subtotal` minus `discount`. On a hosted payment it changes before the payer picks a method when the payer changes a quantity, ticks the order bump or applies a coupon. `0` on a `FREE` payment.

feeAmount.description: YuvexPay platform fee, in BRL. When `feePassedToPayer` is true, this equals `payerFeeAmount` and is charged on top of `amount`. When false, this is deducted from `amount` to produce `netAmount`.

netAmount.description: Merchant's net receivable, in BRL. Equals `amount` when `feePassedToPayer` is true; equals `amount - feeAmount` otherwise. This figure is pre-split: when the payment carries `splits`, the originating company keeps `netAmount` minus the sum of the splits and the rest is credited to the recipients on settlement.

feePassedToPayer.description: Resolved decision (after applying the per-payment override, company default, and sub-R$1 forced passthrough) on whether the fee was added on top for the payer.

payerFeeAmount.description: Fee amount added to the payer's total charge. Null when `feePassedToPayer` is false. When true, payer-charged total = `amount + payerFeeAmount`.

splits.description: Splits recorded on this payment, in the order they were sent. `[]` when the payment has none. Only the originating company can read them: a recipient calling `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` for this payment gets `404`.

methodData.description: Payment method-specific data (QR code for PIX, masked card data for CARD, barcode for boleto). `null` while the payment has no method data: a boleto payment that is `PROCESSING` after a `502`, a card payment that is `PROCESSING` before the outcome of its charge is known, a payment recorded `CANCELLED` or `EXPIRED` before a charge was created, a hosted payment still in `PENDING_METHOD_SELECTION`, or a `FREE` payment. For CARD, `cardFundingType` is `credit` or `debit`, and `null` when the funding type is not known, including older payments.

cardFundingType.description: CARD only. `credit` when the card was charged as a credit card in a single installment, `debit` when it was charged as a debit card. `null` when the funding type is not known, including older payments.

paidAt.description: Timestamp when the payment was confirmed paid. Null until paid, and on a `FREE` payment, which has `completedAt` instead.

completedAt.description: When a `FREE` payment completed. `null` on every other payment.

payer.description: Payer (debtor) identity captured from the PIX network once the charge is paid. Before that, `name` and `document` carry what you sent in `customer`, completed with what the payer typed on the hosted checkout. `email` and `phone` carry the payer's contact. `null` when none of the seven fields is known, for example on historical records or open-payer charges. A `payer` that has only `email` or `phone` is possible, so a non-null `payer` does not mean the payment was paid. Webhook `payer` blocks are unchanged and carry no `email` or `phone`.

document.description: Payer CPF or CNPJ, as digits. Some PIX participants report the document masked (for example `***405566**`); when that is all the network gave us, the masked string is what this field carries — a full document wins whenever one is on file. `null` when no document of either kind was captured, which for an open-payer charge is common. Match on `*` before parsing the value as a CPF or CNPJ.

documentType.description: Payer document type. `null` when the network did not say which kind of document it reported, which is the usual case alongside a masked `document`.

institutionIspb.description: Payer bank ISPB (Banco Central participant identifier).

email.description: Payer e-mail: the one the payer typed on the hosted checkout, else the one in `customer`, or of the customer named in `customerId`, when the payment was created. `GET /v1/payments/{paymentId}` and `POST /v1/payments/{paymentId}/simulate` also fall back to the current e-mail of the customer linked to the payment; `GET /v1/payments` and `GET /v1/payments/txid/{txId}` do not. `null` when not known.

phone.description: Payer phone, with the same sources and fallback as `email`. `null` when not known.

recoveryKit.description: Recovery kit of this payment. See `recoveryKit` on `POST /v1/payments`.

enabled.description: The kit is on for this payment. `false` when the payment was created with the kit off, in sandbox, or before the kit existed, and on a payment-link payment whose payer already has a kit running on that link.

charged.description: The kit price was debited from your balance. It is debited once, when the first e-mail of the kit is sent.

emailsSent.description: Recovery e-mails sent for this payment, including the one sent before a PIX code expires.

items.description: Order lines, `[]` when the payment was created with an amount only, until the payer ticks an order bump.

subtotal.description: Amount before the coupon, in BRL.

discount.description: Coupon discount, in BRL. `0` without a coupon.

parentPaymentId.description: On a payment created by a post-purchase upsell, the payment whose upsell the payer accepted. `null` otherwise.

reason.description: The reason sent with the refund request. `Pedido de reembolso do comprador` on a refund the payer requested and you approved, or that was approved automatically. `Reembolso feito pela YuvexPay` on a refund YuvexPay made after a payer's refund request: it debits the full amount returned to the payer, YuvexPay keeps the processing fee and the balance can go negative. `null` when none was sent and on refunds that reached YuvexPay from the payment network, such as the return of a PIX MED.

txId.description: Transaction identifier: `WIT` followed by a millisecond timestamp and 5 uppercase alphanumerics, e.g. `WIT1746280868443K3F9Q`. Treat it as an opaque string.

pixKey.description: The destination PIX key, masked. The full key is never returned by the API once the withdrawal is created.

pixKeyType.description: Type of PIX key: `CPF`, `CNPJ`, `EMAIL`, `PHONE` or `EVP` (random key).

errorMessage.description: Generic message from the same fixed set as the `WITHDRAWAL_FAILED` webhook `failureReason`, or `Saque em processamento.` while the withdrawal is `PENDING` or `PROCESSING`. `null` when no reason was recorded or the withdrawal is `COMPLETED`.

providerErrorCode.description: Rejection code reported by the receiving institution: `AC03`, `AC06`, `AC07`, `AG03`, `AM18`, `RR04`, `SL02`, `BE01`, `CH11`, `PIX_KEY_NOT_FOUND`, `PIX_KEY_OWNER_MISMATCH`, `ACCOUNT_CLOSED` or `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`. `null` for every other failure and for withdrawals that did not fail.

txId.description: Transaction identifier: `WIT` followed by a millisecond timestamp and 5 uppercase alphanumerics, e.g. `WIT1746280868443K3F9Q`. Treat it as an opaque string.

pixKey.description: The destination PIX key, masked. The full key is never returned by the API once the withdrawal is created.

pixKeyType.description: Type of PIX key: `CPF`, `CNPJ`, `EMAIL`, `PHONE` or `EVP` (random key).

providerErrorCode.description: Rejection code reported by the receiving institution: `AC03`, `AC06`, `AC07`, `AG03`, `AM18`, `RR04`, `SL02`, `BE01`, `CH11`, `PIX_KEY_NOT_FOUND`, `PIX_KEY_OWNER_MISMATCH`, `ACCOUNT_CLOSED` or `ACCOUNT_BLOCKED`. `null` for every other failure and for withdrawals that did not fail.

WithdrawalListItem.description: A withdrawal as returned by `GET /v1/withdrawals`. It carries no `errorMessage` and no `isSandbox`; read `GET /v1/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}` for the failure message.

currentLimit.description: Daily (or nightly, when `isNightTime` is true) limit in BRL.

used.description: Amount already consumed today, in BRL. Counts `amount + feeAmount` of each withdrawal, and is a single counter for the whole Brazilian calendar day — the nightly limit is compared against a total that already includes daytime volume.

remaining.description: Remaining capacity for the current window, in BRL. Because the fee counts towards the limit, the largest `amount` you can request is `remaining - fee`. When a withdrawal ceiling applies to your account, `remaining` never exceeds what that ceiling still allows, and a request above it fails with `400 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, like one above your available balance.

isNightTime.description: Whether reduced night limits are active.

fee.description: Withdrawal fee, a flat amount in BRL charged on top of `amount`. Read it from here rather than hardcoding it: it is configurable per account.

minAmount.description: Minimum withdrawal amount in BRL that applies to your account, compared against `amount` (the net) rather than against `amount + fee`. Never below the `R$ 10.00` platform floor, but it can be higher. Unrelated to the minimum of the PIX route that sends the payout, which surfaces as `WITHDRAWAL_BELOW_PROVIDER_MINIMUM`.

perTransactionLimit.description: Largest single withdrawal your account may request, in BRL, or `null` when no account-level cap applies. Like the daily limit it is compared against `amount + fee`, so the largest `amount` you can request is `perTransactionLimit - fee`. A second, lower ceiling can apply on the PIX route that sends the payout; it depends on live routing and is not returned here, but it is still evaluated synchronously and comes back as a `400 WITHDRAWAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` or `400 WITHDRAWAL_BELOW_PROVIDER_MINIMUM` on the create call.

customerId.description: Merchant-facing customer slug (e.g., `cus_ab12cd34ef`). Use this as the `{customerId}` path parameter in subsequent calls.

code.description: Uppercase code, 3 to 32 characters from `A-Z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`.

percentBp.description: `PERCENT` only: the discount in basis points, `1500` for 15% and `10000` for 100%. `null` on a `FIXED` coupon.

amount.description: `FIXED` only: the discount in BRL. `null` on a `PERCENT` coupon.

validFrom.description: The coupon works from this time on, inclusive. `null`: no start.

validUntil.description: The coupon stops working at this time, exclusive. `null`: no end.

maxRedemptionsPerBuyer.description: Uses per payer e-mail. `null`: no limit.

productIds.description: Products the discount covers. Empty: the whole order.

redemptionCount.description: Uses taken: payments holding the coupon that are still open, plus the completed ones. A payment that expires or is cancelled gives its use back.

FlatError.description: The flat error envelope used by low-level guards that reply before the API error envelope is applied — today the idempotency middleware. The machine-readable code is the top-level `code`; `error` is only the HTTP reason phrase.

statusCode.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

error.description: HTTP reason phrase, for example `Conflict` or `Bad Request`. Not a machine-readable code.

Balance.description: Account balance for the company associated with the API key. The four buckets `available`, `frozen`, `held`, and `reserved` are independent and additive — `total = available + frozen + held + reserved`.

available.description: Settled funds free to use, in BRL. The largest withdrawal you can request right now is also bounded by `remaining` and `perTransactionLimit` from `GET /v1/withdrawals/limits`. This can be negative: when a refund or a PIX MED is apportioned across a split, each recipient is debited its share even if it has already withdrawn the money. A negative balance blocks withdrawals until it is covered by new settlements.

frozen.description: Funds reserved/frozen for in-flight withdrawals, refunds, or operational holds. Not currently withdrawable, but still part of the account balance until the underlying operation reaches a terminal state. Independent from `available`.

held.description: Confirmed amount pending settlement (for example, card or boleto payments confirmed but not yet liquidated). Will move to `available` once settled.

reserved.description: Rolling reserve: a share of settled funds withheld when your account is subject to a reserve policy, released back to `available` on each release date. Not currently withdrawable, and not usable to fund a refund you issue, until released. A split credit received from another YuvexPay company follows your own reserve policy, not the originating company's; when a refund or MED debit lands on a split share that is still reserved, that payment's own reserve hold is released first and the debit is written against it. `0` when no reserve applies.

total.description: Total account balance: `available + frozen + held + reserved`.

currency.description: Always `BRL`. Multi-currency is not yet supported on the public API.

environment.description: Environment of the API key used to make this call. Sandbox keys always return zeros.

updatedAt.description: When the balance row was last updated. `null` if the company has never had any balance activity.

name.description: Human-readable name set in the dashboard.

environment.description: Environment the key is bound to.

prefix.description: The non-secret prefix of the key (`ypk_<env>_<kid>`). Safe to log.

ipAllowlist.description: List of allowed IPs/CIDRs. Empty means no restriction.

rateLimitPerMinute.description: Per-key rate limit in requests per minute, or null for the account default.

expiresAt.description: Expiration timestamp, or null if the key does not expire.

netAmount.description: Merchant's net receivable, pre-split. When the payment carries `splits`, the originating company keeps `netAmount` minus the sum of the splits.

feePassedToPayer.description: Resolved decision on whether the fee was added on top for the payer.

payerFeeAmount.description: Fee added to payer's total when `feePassedToPayer` is true; null otherwise.

splits.description: Splits recorded on this payment, in the order they were sent. `[]` when the payment has none.

methodData.description: Method-specific data. PIX returns QR data. BOLETO returns the digitable line and barcode. CARD returns masked card data and `cardFundingType`, only when the request returns an existing card payment. `null` when the request returns an existing boleto payment that is `PROCESSING` after a `502`, one recorded `CANCELLED` before a charge was created, or a payment created as `FREE`.

WebhookPayerBlock.description: Payer block. `null` when every field would be null.

name.description: Payer name as reported by the settling institution.

document.description: Payer CPF or CNPJ, as digits, or a masked string (for example `***405566**`) when no full document is on file. `null` when neither was captured. Match on `*` before parsing the value as a CPF or CNPJ.

WebhookRecipientBlock.description: Recipient block. `null` when every field would be null. There is no `documentType` here, unlike `payer`.

name.description: Recipient name as reported by the settling institution.

document.description: Recipient CPF or CNPJ. Populated when the withdrawal was created with `destination.recipientDocument`, or with a CPF or CNPJ `destination.pixKey`, or when the receiving account was reported back after the transfer. `null` otherwise.

branch.description: Recipient branch, when it is reported back.

account.description: Recipient account, when it is reported back.

This response is deliberately narrower than `GET /v1/withdrawals/{withdrawalId}`: it omits `pixKey`, `pixKeyType`, `processedAt`, `errorMessage` and `providerErrorCode`, which are only meaningful once the network has acted.

id.description: Identifier of the relationship, not of the company.

companyId.description: Company ID of the counterparty. This is the value to send as `recipientCompanyId` in `splits[]`.

feeCap.description: Fee cap recorded on the relationship when the recipient is an approved split platform: the most it may take of each payment, in percent of `amount`, as a string with two decimal places. `null` for an ordinary partner. IdempotencyConflict.description: Idempotency conflict, raised by the idempotency middleware. `IDEMPOTENCY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH` means the key was already used with a different request body, at any point in the 24-hour window, including by a request still in flight. `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` means a request with the same key and the same body is still being processed. Both use the **flat** envelope: `error` is the HTTP reason phrase and the machine-readable code is the top-level `code`. Note that `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` raised later by the withdrawal service on an idempotency-key collision uses the nested `Error` envelope instead.
